title: Kakao, OpenAI Collaborate on AI-Generated Short Animation Based on Ryan Begins Webtoon
content:
Kakao announced on November 10 that it has produced Ryan Begins , the first AI short animation starring its popular character Ryan, through a technology collaboration with OpenAI.

Based on the the webtoon of the same name, the approximately seven-minute short combines human creative direction with generative AI tools in its planning and production.

The production team includes director Jiwon Han, who directed Netflix 's animated film Lost in Starlight , and AI supervisor Young-jun Kim. The team used ChatGPT's image generation feature to create initial images based on scene sketches and detailed prompts. Artists then manually refined and revised the images to achieve the intended visual quality.

According to the production team, they used approximately 1,500 prompts for a single scene to achieve the desired direction and emotional tone.

Kakao held a special advance screening and a Q&A session on November 8 at Movieland in Seongsu-dong, Seoul. The event also featured an exhibition showcasing the animation's production process. Tickets for the Q&A session sold out within a day of going on sale.

Han said the team focused on conveying Ryan's emotions without relying on dialogue or exaggerated facial expressions, allowing viewers to find their own interpretations of the story. Kim added that the team repeatedly revised AI-generated images whenever they did not match the intended emotional tone, emphasizing that the creators' decisions and hands-on work determined the final result.

The webtoon launched last year and features the Kakao Friends character Ryan. Unlike previous slice-of-life webtoons featuring Kakao Friends, this series marked the first official storyline-driven webtoon that builds on Ryan's universe.

An English version of the original webtoon is not available.
author: ANN

title: Bleach Creator Returns With New Look at Ichigo After Anime’s Finale
content:
Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War wrapped up the anime’s two decade long run with its final episodes earlier this Fall, and the creator behind it all is helping to celebrate with some special new art for Ichigo Kurosaki. It took 22 years to get to that point, but Bleach fans were finally able to see the final arc from Kubo’s original manga in action with a proper anime adaptation. And the anime really went all out for the grand finale given that it’s taken so long to get there.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War wrapped up with the anime’s final two episodes last month, and the final episode of the series ushered Ichigo and the others off into a bright future ten years after the fight against Yhwach . It was a big finale for a number of reasons, but also because fans saw one final look at Ichigo. But now Kubo has taken to social media to share a cool new sketch of Ichigo to help commemorate the anime’s finale too. You can check it out below.

Bleach Creator Shares New Look at Ichigo After Anime Finale

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War capped off the TV anime’s run after 22 long years with the release of Episode 50 earlier this Fall . But there are still some fans who have yet to see the final episodes for themselves. Because while the the Japanese language release is now streaming with Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ as of this time (along with the entire original series), the English dub release of the final has yet to make its own debut. Thankfully it won’t be too much longer as the English dub will be ending its run later this month.

The English dub release for Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Episode 49 will be debuting with Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ on November 23rd at 8:30AM PT, and then it will be followed by the release of Episode 50 on November 30th at 8:30AM PT. So while the anime has indeed come to an end, there’s still a fresh way fans will be able to watch the series to say goodbye all over again. But while this is the end of the story for now, it’s far from the actual end of Bleach ‘s original manga story overall.

What’s Next for Bleach ?

Tite Kubo previously returned to Bleach a few years ago with a special one-shot manga that actually picked up some time after the original finale. Exploring more of the new Soul Reapers that have popped up over the years along with featuring a slightly older version of Ichigo’s son Kazui, this one-shot was also the start of a whole new arc with a new region threatening to encroach on the others. This is a major story with the potential of getting its own anime adaptation someday.

It’s yet to be revealed whether or not Bleach’ s Hell Arc will be coming to the anime, but it’s something fans are definitely hoping to see revealed when the franchise comes back next year for a major event. Bleach Fes is coming to Japan this February and it will feature members from the voice cast as they celebrate ending it after 22 long years , but that would be the perfect time to reveal a potential future.

How did you feel about Bleach’ s anime finale? Would you want to see the franchise come back for more someday? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: My Hero Academia Reveals First Look at Major Event for the Anime’s Grand Finale
content:
My Hero Academia is coming back with a major event to cap off the anime’s tenth anniversary celebration, and now fans have gotten the first look at the new event as it gears up for the anime’s grand finale. Though the franchise wrapped up the final season of the TV anime series last year and through some special new releases through the Spring and Summer, there’s still one big event planned to help commemorate the franchise’s decade long history on air thus far in a cool way.

My Hero Academia Ultra Expo has been announced as a major event coming to Japan next Spring that will be featuring members of the voice cast and more as a way to finish off the 10th anniversary celebration for the TV anime in style. The event has yet to reveal more about exactly what fans in the area will be able to enjoy when it hits, but the first poster for it has been revealed. You can check it out below.

My Hero Academia Ultra Expo 2027 Official Poster Revealed

My Hero Academia Ultra Expo will be taking place on April 17-18 in Japan next year, but unfortunately it’s not likely going to be available to fans in international territories. It’s yet to be revealed what kind of events are planned for the new expo as of this time, but it’s all been teased to be an ultimate celebration of the anime’s tenth anniversary after everything that went down this year. There have been a number of major projects released through the year thus far, and each one has been notable in its own way such as the new anime continuations.

Because while My Hero Academia ended its TV anime run last year, it returned for a special epilogue episode earlier this Spring that helped to expand on everything that happened in the time skip seen with that original finale. Spending more time with Izuku Midoriya and the others in their pro hero futures , this was then further extended with one final short that adapted the final materials from Kohei Horikoshi’s original manga release. This seemingly means that it’s all truly ended now with nothing more on the horizon. That doesn’t have to be the case, however.

Is My Hero Academia’ s Anime Really Over?

My Hero Academia might have adapted the final materials left by Horikoshi, and the creator himself has already moved onto new projects in Shonen Jump , there’s clearly still a ton of interest in the franchise. The anime team has been keeping the project alive with new celebrations and releases, and this new expo is just another example of it. If there were any plans to reveal for the future of the series, this would be the perfect time to reveal those plans.

My Hero Academia is one of the major franchises that Shueisha will be showcasing as part of their upcoming Jump Festa 2027 event later this December , and there’s a chance something could be revealed there too. The time skip period seen in the anime’s finale is just perfect for a potential exploration of an original project with a fun final original story, but we’ll have to see if that’s in the cards. Are you hoping to see My Hero Academia ‘s anime return someday? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Shonen Jump Shares First Look at Major Creator’s Return After 3 Years
content:
A major creator is returning to the pages of Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine with a new series after three years, and Shonen Jump has dropped the first look at their next major project. Shonen Jump is now entering its final phase of shifting its releases around for the year with some long running franchises coming to their respective ends. But with the end of some of its longer running series (and potentially more cancellations), it makes room for newer series to take their place in turn .

It’s been announced that Kenta Shinohara’s Witch Watch is coming to an end with its next chapter , and now it’s been revealed that the next major series taking its place comes from returning creator Ryo Nakama. Last seen with Shonen Jump with the end of High School Family: Kokosei Kazoku back in 2023, Nakama is now back in action with a new series titled Jan Is in Danger! You can check out the first look at Nakama’s new series below ahead of its full debut this weekend.

Jan Is in Danger! Reveals First Look Ahead of Shonen Jump Debut

Jan Is in Danger! is the next major series from Ryo Nakama making its debut with the next issue of Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine this weekend, and the first look at the new series teases a parody much in line with what had been seen with Nakama before. Outside of this mysterious visual teasing a main character who seemingly is unaware of the explosion happening behind him, the series is teased as such, “He’s the most happy-go-lucky teen around, but he also happens to be the toughest guy in town!” And there’s a hope it matches up to High School Family: Kokosei Kazoku ‘s own success.

High School Family: Kokosei Kazoku made its initial debut in 2020, and ran with the magazine for three years before coming to an end in 2023. It’s not exactly that the series had been cancelled, but instead just sort of ran out of steam in terms of what it was trying to do. There might be the same kind of ceiling on yet another gag series, but we’ll have to see when the manga itself makes its full chapter debut. But even then, Nakama’s previous work is coming back for more too .

What’s Next for High School Family ?

High School Family: Kokosei Kazoku is one of the next Shonen Jump franchises to get its own live-action feature film adaptation . Coming to theaters across Japan next January, the new movie is directed by Toichiro Ruto with a script from Europe Kikaku’s Makoto Ueda. It’s not exactly the most popular series to ever run with Shonen Jump , but it’s got the kind of idea that’s going to be perfect for new adaptations like this one. Unfortunately as of this time, no international release plans have been announced for the film.

This is the first of three new titles scheduled to come to Shonen Jump through the rest of the month, and will be the final wave of new entries for the magazine this year. There have been a number of long running hits that have come to their respective ends, so it just remains to be seen which of the titles will be ending their stories next. But are you excited for Ryo Nakama’s return to Shonen Jump ? Let us know your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: South Park Just Retconned a Major Character With Their Return & It’s a Big Improvement
content:
South Park Season 29 has gone back on a major character change made last year, and it is a big improvement as PC Principal is now back to his more classic self with the latest episode. South Park Season 29 has been more of a return to form to the earlier seasons of the animated series. Rather than be solely focused on United States President Donald Trump as seen with Seasons 27 and 28 last year, it’s almost as if the series has been distancing itself with a course correction .

Like with the change of the series’ name and town to “South America” for Season 29, South Park has made some notable changes to many of its other characters and storylines that have essentially been shifting away from all of the changes made last year. But one of the biggest comes with the latest episode as PC Principal has been returned to his formerly “Politically Correct” self rather than the “Power Christian” version of the character he had been turned into last year.

PC Principal Returns in South Park Season 29 With Major Changes

South Park Season 29 has decisively shifted much of its focus away from Trump and the political stories that had been dominating the animated series last year, but has been indirectly addressing it through its equating the release of Grand Theft Auto VI to the midterm elections changing the country . But with the elections now passed ahead of the newest episode, series creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone address this directly once more as Mr. Garrison officially reintroduces PC Principal back as his older self and not the “Power Christian” he had turned into last season.

With Garrison remarking “Of course we could just go on and on and make a bunch of jokes about him” and noting how the series was just not going to do that this episode. Instead Garrison reveals that the school will be enacting “liberal changes ” with PC Principal back in the fold and celebrating the fact that he’s returned to his older self. With PC Principal even saying he’s been “messed up the past couple of years,” and is planning to get things back on track. It’s a great move forward going back on all of the changes that just had not been working with the character before.

What Does This Mean for South Park ‘s Future?

South Park is in an interesting place as Season 29 now reaches its finale. Ever since it changed its name to “South America,” there was a worry that it would be once again dominated by all of the political stories and side characters like seen with last year. Instead each of the episodes thus far have been a pointed return to the core characters with the boys and their immediate circle getting the bulk of the stories seen with this season thus far.

It seems that while focusing so much on Trump last year ended up with some of the most watched episodes of South Park in a long time, the series has bounced from that idea and is just focusing more on the characters themselves . It’s resulted in some great work so far, but we’ll have to see what it means for the finale. How are you liking all of these changes in South Park Season 29 so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Classroom of the Elite: Year 3 Tops Oricon's Light Novel Ranking for October
content:
The anime adaptation's fourth and latest season debuted on April 1 and covers the first semester of the Year 2 light novels. The anime will get a fifth season .

The second volume of Kinoko Nasu and illustrator Hirokazu Koyama 's Witch on the Holy Night novel series ranked at #2, selling 30,534 copies. The volume shipped on September 30. The first volume shipped on August 27 and ranked at #3 on Oricon's light novel ranking chart for August. The Witch on the Holy Night anime film will open in Japan on November 20. The original visual novel game's smartphone version will also launch simultaneously on November 20.

The 12th volume of Sunsunsun and illustrator Momoco 's Alya Sometimes Hides Her Feelings in Russian light novel series ranked at #3, selling 23,197 copies. The volume shipped on October 1. Yen Press releases the novels in English. The second anime season based on the novels will debut next year after a delay from this year.

About ORICON:

ORICON is a company that provides rankings and news. Since 1967, it has been compiling data on record sales in Japan and publishing rankings; since 2008, it has also published the “ORICON Book Ranking” based on sales figures. The company holds a vast amount of data on the Japanese entertainment market. It operates “ORICON NEWS,” Japan's largest entertainment website, and runs “Japan Anime News” as its global version.

title: Kagurabachi Drops Cool New Look at Chihiro’s Anime Debut
content:
Kagurabachi is setting itself up as one of the biggest new anime to make their worldwide debuts next year, and it’s getting even cooler with a much closer look at Chihiro Rokuhira ahead of his big outing. Takeru Hokazono’s Kagurabachi has been one of the most successful new stories to come out of Shonen Jump in the last few years, and that’s likely going to be an even bigger deal when the franchise gets its official TV anime adaptation. Making its debut next Spring, it’s been on a world tour to help celebrate .

Kagurabachi will be making its worldwide premiere next Spring and has been steadily revealing more of what fans can expect from the new anime over the past few months. Now fans have gotten a much closer look at Chihiro with a new character poster showing off his various expressions that will be on display. You can check it out below for a fresh look at Chihiro.

When Does Kagurabachi ‘s Anime Come Out?

Kagurabachi will be making its worldwide debut sometime next April as part of the Spring 2027 anime schedule. No concrete release date has been announced for the series as of this time, but it has been confirmed that the anime will be streaming with Crunchyroll when it finally hits . There are still many details about the anime left to be revealed such as its production staff, but it will be directed by Tetsuya Takeuchi for Cypic with Keigo Sasaki providing the character designs. Though the rest of the staff has yet to be confirmed.

The first additions to the voice cast for Kagurabachi have been revealed, however. The new series will be starring the likes of Taihi Kimura as Chihiro Rokuhira, Tomokazu Seki as Kunishige Rokuhira, Katsuyuki Konishi as Togo Shiba, Miyari Nemoto as Char Kyonagi, Miku Ito as Hinao , and Yuichi Nakamura as Soshiro Azami. There are also likely a lot more characters to be revealed, but fans will see soon enough given that it’s not going to be much longer before the anime is fully up and running beyond its special world tour for the first episode.

When Will Kagurabachi Reveal Its Next Anime Update?

Kagurabachi has been on a special world tour for the past few months as it has shared an early preview of its first episode at some of the biggest anime conventions and events through the year. title: Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 Confirms Episode Release Schedule for 2027 Launch
content:
Avatar: Seven Havens has not only confirmed Season 2’s release date ahead of its return in 2027, but the animated series has also revealed the release schedule for all of its future episodes. When Avatar: Seven Havens was first confirmed to be on the way to Paramount+, it was revealed to be slated for 26 episodes at the time spread across two seasons. The initial worry ahead of its launch was that all episodes would be released at once, and thankfully that wasn’t the case for the first season.

Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ debut season was released over the month of October on Paramount+ with a few episodes releasing each wee k, and now the streaming service has confirmed that it will be the same case for Season 2’s episodes when it makes its debut next Spring. Coming to Paramount+ next May, Avatar: Seven Havens Book 2 will be rolling out on the streaming service on a weekly basis with a few episodes dropping each week through the month.

Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 Confirms Paramount+ Release Schedule

Avatar: Seven Havens Book 2 will be 13 episodes in total (much like the first season), and Episodes 1-3 will be making their worldwide debut with Paramount+ on May 21st next year. It will then be followed by the release of Episodes 4-6 on May 28th, Episodes 7-9 on June 4th, and the final batch of Episodes 10-13 on June 11th. Officially given the title of “Book Two: Discovery,” the next season of the animated series will be picking up right from that first season cliffhanger as Pavi heads to the next Haven.

You’ll want to catch up with everything that’s happened in Avatar: Seven Havens with Paramount+ in the meantime as Pavi is heading out of Ellora to seek out the Floating Isles. After tapping into her latent Rook Chakra abilities at the end of the first season, Pavi discovers that her path forward is heading to the other Havens in order to learn more about the other six chakra abilities hiding within her . All the while Nisha has some troubles of her own to deal with.

What to Know for Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2

Avatar: Seven Havens Book 2 will feature a returning voice cast with the likes of Saheli Khan as Pavi, Aishu Devan as Nisha, Akshay Khanna as Karthik, Major Curda as Jae, Sakina Jaffrey as Agam, Darren Barnet as Daemin, and Dee Bradley Baker as Geet and Ruhi. Potential new additions to the cast as the world around Pavi and Nisha expands have yet to be revealed as of this time, but we’re about to find out much more about the state of this post-apocalyptic world at large .

Avatar: Seven Havens has also announced that Seasons 3 and 4 are already in production with the third season coming later in 2027 too. This series has also been confirmed by those behind the scenes that it will only be running for four seasons in total to tell its full story , so it seems like it’s all happening relatively quickly in the near future. How do you feel about the release schedule for Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ return in 2027? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Crunchyroll’s Biggest Isekai Confirms Season 5 Return With First Look
content:
One of the biggest Isekai franchises now streaming with Crunchyroll has now confirmed it’s coming back for Season 5 in the near future. The anime adaptation for Tappei Nagatsuki and Shinichirou Otsuka has been on an incredible run for the past decade as it now celebrates its 10th anniversary. The series made its comeback with its fourth season earlier this Summer, and wrapped up its run without any word on a potential return . But thankfully the future has been set in place not long after.

Re:Zero -Starting Life in Another World- fans thankfully didn’t have to wait too long to find out whether or not the anime would be continuing as it has now been officially announced that the anime is now in production on Season 5. During a special event in Japan this weekend to help celebrate the 10th anniversary of the TV anime’s original debut, Re:Zero -Starting Life in Another World- has now confirmed Season 5 is in the works with the first look at the coming episodes. You can check it out below.

Re:Zero Season 5 Officially Announced

Re:Zero -Starting Life in Another World- Season 5 has now been confirmed to officially be in production, but unfortunately no concrete release date or window has been revealed as of this time. Potential production staff or returning voice cast have yet to be revealed as of this time either, but it’s going to be picking up right after that finale. With Subaru overcoming all of the challenges of the Loss and Recapture Arcs seen in the fourth season, Rem has finally woken up from her coma and is set to be an active part in the series once more.

On congratulating the anime franchise for making it to its fifth season, original series creator Tappei Nagatsuki teased a bit of the brutal journey that Subaru is about to embark on in Season 5. As for what’s coming, it turns out Re:Zero -Starting Life in Another World- is about to get even more intense than what happened before , “The sixth arc covered in Season 4 has been called one of the most difficult parts of Re:ZERO , but don’t worry! The journey through the seventh arc is every bit as brutal, with the difficulty cranked all the way up to inferno.”

What’s Next for Re:Zero Season 5?

“The story continues with the same reassuringly heart-breaking design you’ve come to expect—yes, ‘heart-breaking’ is intentional!” Nagatsuki continues to tease about the coming season. “Of course, it won’t all be hardship. There will also be plenty of new encounters, exciting developments, and scenes I can’t wait to see—and show you—in anime form!” With all sorts of wild events already going down, it’s hard to imagine how it’s going to get even wilder for Subaru in the coming season.

With Rem now fully back in the picture, but seemingly without any of her memories of her time with Subaru, the two of them need to find a connection once more in this new circumstance. They have been separated from everyone else with that cliffhanger, so make sure to catch up with it all now streaming with Crunchyroll with both Japanese and English language audio in the meantime . Are you excited for Re:Zero Season 5? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Love Live! Hasu no Sora Jogakuin School Idol Club Anime's Special Video Previews TV Footage
content:
The " Love Live! Series 15th Anniversary Love Live! Fes" presented a special promotional video for the television anime of the Love Live! Hasu no Sora Jogakuin School Idol Club project on Saturday. The video previews the newly animated television footage for the first time, and it also previews the song "Dream Believers (106th Class Start Ver.)" by the in-story 106th class of Hasu no Sora Joga kuin School Idol Club.

The anime will show the characters of the 106th class in stories set between April and June of their school year. (The game and anime film previously only featured characters from the 103rd to 105th class.)

Gō Kurosaki ( Shikizakura ) is directing the project at Sublimation . Fumiaki Maruto ( Engage Kiss , SI-VIS: The Sound of Heroes , White Album 2 ) is writing the scripts. Haruko Iizuka ( Ensemble Stars! , Tamayura ) is designing the characters, Kaito Hamakawa is directing the CG, Keiichi Nozaki ( Ongaku Shōjo , L/R: Licensed by Royalty ) is directing the sound, and Yoshiaki Fujisawa ( Apocalypse Hotel , Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation ) is composing the music with Lantis handling music production.

Other staff members include:

• Design Works: Yū Kisaragi

• Art Director: Yasuhiro Okumura

• Stage Concept Art: Marina Manode

• Color Key Artist: Hikari Komiya

• Compositing Director of Photography: Fumika Takahashi, Hiroshi Tanaka

• Editing: Manabu Kamino

The staff remains mostly the same as the Love Live! Hasu no Sora Jogakuin School Idol Club Bloom Garden Party anime film, with the exception of Hikari Komiya as the color key artist (replacing Emi Chiba ), and the addition of Fumika Takahashi as compositing director of photography alongside the returning Hiroshi Tanaka .

The seven-episode anime will premiere on January 10 at 10:30 p.m. (8:30 a.m. EST) on the Tokyo MX channel, followed by BS11 , Sun TV , KBS Kyoto , TV Aichi , RKB Mainichi Broadcasting , and Shizuoka Broadcasting System later that day. It will also run on January 11 on Hokkaido Broadcasting, and on January 17 on Hokuriku Broadcasting .

The Love Live! Hasu no Sora Jogakuin School Idol Club Bloom Garden Party 3D anime film opened in theaters in Japan on May 8. The film follows the final day before graduation of the 103rd class at the Hasu no Sora Girls' Academy.

The " Hasu no Sora Jōgakuin School Idol Club " idol group is part of the Love Live! franchise , and includes Kaho Hinoshita, Sayaka Murano, Kozue Otomune, Tsuzuri Yugiri, Rurino Osawa, and Megumi Fujishima, among others. The group is primarily featured in the Link! Like! Love Live! smartphone game app, which launched on April 15, 2023. Haruko Iizuka ( Little Busters! , Horimiya ) is designing the characters for the project. Odd No. Inc. is publishing the game. The group's first album Dream Believers debuted on March 29, 2023.

The game ended service on June 30 earlier this year. Odd No. filed for bankruptcy on August 5.

The project lets fans experience the story "together with school idols over 365 days" and let players "walk the path to graduation with the girls." In addition to the smartphone app, the idol club members (and their cast) stream videos, appear in magazines, release music CDs, hold concerts, among other efforts in various forms of media. A manga launched in Shueisha 's Ultra Jump magazine in November 2023.

The Love Live! school idol franchise launched in 2010 and has since spawned the Love Live! Sunshine!! , Love Live! Nijigasaki High School Idol Club , Love Live! Superstar!! and most recently, Ikizu Live! Love Live! Bluebird project spinoffs.
